Riyadh has increased the use of the 745-mile pipeline since the start of the war on Iran in order to bypass the strait of Hormuz’s closure. The world’s biggest exporter has used the pipeline to reroute about 4m barrels a day – about 4% of global supply – but with the ‌pipeline out of service, the Red Sea port of Yanbu now has stocks to maintain exports for just five to seven days.

events.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
events.summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

events.title: Chancellor Merz says AfD result 'changes all of Germany'
events.summary: A visibly shaken but also determined Friedrich Merz spoke in Berlin about the AfD's election victory in Saxony-Anhalt and the CDU's bitter defeat. He insisted on sticking to his reforms.

events.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
events.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

events.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Digesting the AfD's landmark election win
events.summary: With well over 40% for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), Saxony-Anhalt has witnessed a landmark election night. DW's reporters were on the ground.

events.title: Fact check: Election fraud claims spread in Saxony-Anhalt
events.summary: False and misleading claims are raising questions about the integrity of the election in Saxony-Anhalt. DW Fact Check takes a closer look.

events.title: Germany set to feel the impact of Saxony-Anhalt's AfD win
events.summary: The state election could have major consequences for Germany's government. Pollsters cite dissatisfaction with Merz as one reason for the CDU's poor showing.

events.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
events.summary: The AfD has emerged as the strongest party in Germany's eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt by a wide margin. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

events.title: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
events.summary: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

events.title: Germany plans anti-drone shield over Leipzig attack — report
events.summary: Several German cities will receive rapidly deployable units capable of defending against drone strikes on critical infrastructure, according to Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

events.title: Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
events.summary: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

events.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
events.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

events.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
events.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. But over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

events.title: Germany news: Thousands march at Saxony-Anhalt rallies
events.summary: Ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's state election on Sunday, a democracy festival by civil society groups has been held in Magdeburg. The far-right AfD organized its final campaign rally in the state capital.

events.title: What would an AfD government in Saxony-Anhalt really mean?
events.summary: Detention centers for deportation, mandatory work for asylum-seekers, vigilante groups — the AfD wants to drastically overhaul Saxony-Anhalt. What does the party have planned?

events.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
events.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

events.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers
events.summary: The far-right AfD has good odds of winning an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament this state election, enabling them to govern alone. It all depends on whether other parties make the cut.

events.title: Germany's civil society alliance takes on the far right
events.summary: Trade unions, churches and human rights activists are worried about the rise of the far-right AfD. How can civil society protect people who are threatened by far-right extremism?

events.title: How vulnerable is Germany's infrastructure?
events.summary: The growing number of attacks on substations and railway lines in Germany is raising concern. Experts say that people will have to get used to the likelihood that such incidents will continue.

events.title: Majority of Germans see Russia as a threat
events.summary: More than half of German citizens believe that Germany's security is threatened by Russia, according to the latest survey by public broadcaster ARD.

events.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
events.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

events.title: Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
events.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

events.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?
events.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party has long claimed that the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind. Is that really the case? A closer look at the data offers some interesting insights.

events.title: Why North Korea's women's football team is so good
events.summary: North Korea's young footballers enter the U-20 World Cup in Poland as defending champions — the 2024 title was their third. Why is the isolated state so good at the game?

events.title: 2026 Beethoven Festival evokes a sense of home
events.summary: The motto of this year's classical music festival in Bonn is "Home/At Home," featuring musicians from diverse cultures presenting pieces from their homelands.

events.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
events.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

events.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
events.summary: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

events.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
events.summary: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

events.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
events.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

events.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
events.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

events.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
events.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

events.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
events.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

events.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response
events.summary: Any escalation in the Baltic region will lead to a significant response, Moscow said.

events.title: Germany says Russia behind attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
events.summary: Investigators believe an explosives-laden drone was deliberately targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August. The German government said on Tuesday that it held Russia "responsible."

events.title: Can communities be protected from melting glaciers?
events.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

events.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
events.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

events.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage
events.summary: With works about Gaza, Ukraine and Elon Musk, political cinema is in the spotlight at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

events.title: Canada's Carney holds firm against Trump tariffs
events.summary: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.

events.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom
events.summary: A quiet multimillion‑dollar black market is exploding across the Indian Ocean, driven by one unlikely animal: the sea cucumber.

events.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
events.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

events.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire
events.summary: The EU wants to lift a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air, allowing drones to be used for greater precision. But experts warn the plan could lead to even more pesticides being used in agriculture.

events.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers
events.summary: She's young and she says what she thinks: Caroline Wahl is topping Germany's bestseller lists with her novels. But she has also faced a public backlash.

events.title: What 'The Odyssey' can teach us about climate chaos
events.summary: The Bronze Age collapse may have started with a water crisis. The droughts of today raise the unsettling question of whether it could happen again.

events.title: Influential humanists: These are the winners of the Goethe Medal 2026
events.summary: The prestigious German cultural award recognizes the artistic work and commitment to cultural dialogue of Arvo Pärt, Anita Raja and Prodromos Tsinikoris.

events.title: Germany's military wants to recruit tech-savvy gamers
events.summary: The Bundeswehr has been a fixture at Gamescom, Cologne's video game trade fair, for years. But critics say military recruitment does not belong at an entertainment convention.

events.title: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum
events.summary: One of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections has been swiped, almost in its entirety, from Villena Museum. A highly professional group of thieves were in and out in four minutes flat before the museum opened.

events.title: Tragedy in Nepal: How do flash floods happen?
events.summary: When flash floods sweep through the Himalayas, there is often little time to react. Scientists are working to understand the risks and improve early warning systems.

events.title: Andre Rankel named Germany's new men's ice hockey coach
events.summary: Germany's men's ice hockey team has appointed a new head coach following a string of dissappointing tournaments. He's two decades younger than the man he's replacing but he has no previous experience as a head coach.

events.title: New study shows German football remains male-dominated
events.summary: The top leagues of German football remain a largely male environment. A new study reveals that only seven clubs have women in upper management levels.

events.title: Venus' US Open invitation raises questions about wild cards
events.summary: Although her current world ranking wouldn't allow it, Venus Williams is set to play singles in the US Open – thanks to a wild card. Who gets these coveted spots—and how?

events.title: The great lake divide: Collapse vs. comeback
events.summary: As some of the world's biggest lakes vanish in real time, others are proving that recovery is still within reach.

events.title: Why social media addiction is so hard to regulate
events.summary: Facebook, Instagram and other social media platforms are accused of deliberately fostering addictive behavior among young users. Yet regulators continue to struggle to rein in their engagement-driven business models.

events.title: Bundesliga season 2026-27: All you need to know
events.summary: From key dates to rising football stars and changes, DW has the latest on the new Bundesliga season.

events.title: Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama dies at 97
events.summary: From works of "self-obliteration" to polka dotted nudes, the pioneering artist developed a unique body of work likely to be relevant for years to come.

events.title: Was the heat of this summer really 'normal?'
events.summary: Some political messaging denies the role of human-caused climate change in this summer's extreme heat. The science tells a different story.

events.title: Tim Curry, of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' dies at 80
events.summary: The gender-bending role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter put Curry on the map in 1975. He then went on to play a number of villainous roles like Gomez Addams, Pennywise and Bill Sikes, but also Mozart and William Shakespeare.

events.title: Reports: UEFA backs off FIFA boycott threat
events.summary: UEFA is reportedly set to withdraw a threat to boycott FIFA tournaments over a plan to partially privatize football tournaments. The Under-20 Women's World Cup is to be hosted by Poland next month.

events.title: Gamescom 2026: What's next for the gaming industry?
events.summary: As Gamescom 2026 opens in Cologne, AI, hardware costs and slowing user growth are putting pressure on the global games industry despite its current strength.

events.title: Remembering Dolly Parton: 8 facts about the icon
events.summary: Dolly Parton, one of the world's most successful artists, has died at the age of 80. Here are some important and extraordinary facts about the country music superstar.

events.title: US country music legend Dolly Parton dies aged 80
events.summary: Representatives of the country music legend told US media that Dolly Parton died after a "brief battle with cancer." Parton's career spans more than half a century and includes a wide array of smash hits.

events.title: Schalke coach looks to Bosnia bond in Bundesliga return
events.summary: After three seasons in the second division, Schalke are back in the Bundesliga. Just a year ago, few would have guessed that their revival would largely be 'Made in Bosnia.'

events.title: Why Germany's Volkswagen could cut 100,000 jobs
events.summary: Europe's biggest automaker, Volkswagen, faces Chinese competition, high costs and US tariffs. What could its restructuring mean for the German car industry?

events.title: Can new US sanctions cripple Iran's shadow economy?
events.summary: The US is expanding sanctions on Iran's financial networks, targeting crypto, gold, aviation and shipping. DW spoke with analysts about what could change.

events.title: Trees are vital for cooler cities, but they need help too
events.summary: Record-breaking heat and drought are putting urban trees at risk. Experts explain how to protect these essential assets and build city forests that can withstand the climate challenges ahead.

events.title: The new Bundesliga season is here, but has the glow gone?
events.summary: Another Bundesliga season arrives, but are the golden years of Germany's top football league already over, and what can it do to change its course?

events.title: Star violinist Anne-Sophie Mutter: 50 years on stage
events.summary: Anne-Sophie Mutter constantly reinvents herself. For her 50th onstage anniversary, the star violinist is surprising audiences with sounds from around the world and never-before-recorded commissions.

events.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
events.summary: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

events.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
events.summary: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

events.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
events.summary: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

events.title: 'Masha and the Bear': Ukraine sanctions Russian cartoon
events.summary: Ukraine has imposed sanctions on the hit Russian children's cartoon "Masha and the Bear," a step towards banning it. The culture minister called the show propaganda. Russia said the move showed Kyiv's "ugly nature."

events.title: Bauhaus Manifesto: Broad alliance promoting artistic freedom
events.summary: Weeks before Saxony-Anhalt's state election, representatives from German cultural, crafts, architecture, design and church sectors unite to promote freedom, openness and creativity.

events.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
events.summary: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier.

events.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
events.summary: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.

events.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
events.summary: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.

events.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern Munich
events.summary: Bernadette Amani is heading into her first full season with Bayern Munich, having joined the club in January. Making a living at football is something she never imagined possible while growing up in rural Ivory Coast.

events.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
events.summary: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

events.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
events.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
events.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

events.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
events.summary: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

events.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
events.summary: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

events.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
events.summary: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.

events.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble
events.summary: The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?

events.title: Can the cool north handle a surge in climate tourism?
events.summary: With heat records continually being broken and southern summers getting hotter, travelers are heading north. Fragile ecosystems are paying the price.

events.title: Fatty food raises risk of colorectal cancer
events.summary: Did you know fatty foods can increase production of an acid in your gut that promotes tumor growth? That's on top of all the other health risks linked to fatty foods, like fries and burgers.

events.title: Countries turn to coal to avoid shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: The US-Israel war on Iran has shaken global energy markets and coal is no exception. Countries around the world are turning to the highly polluting source of power in a bid to avoid shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. According to the International Energy Agency, global coal demand is forecast to rise by ​1.2% this year to a record 8.94 billion ‌tonnes. FRANCE 24’s Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe has the details in this edition.

events.title: Keziah Jones goes symphonic
events.summary: This week arts24 talks to Nigerian Blues Funk Artist Keziah Jones ahead of his Symphonic premier at la Scène Musicale on September 29 as part of Jazz & Musique du Monde season. He tells FRANCE 24's Marjorie Hache about his music and about working with arranger Pierre Bertrand. Plus, we take a look at new releases by Beck, Miley Cyrus and Beabadobee.

events.title: How will EU respond to Russian attack on train near Polish border?
events.summary: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. "It is clearly meant to scare Western countries from supporting Ukraine, from going to Ukraine to show support," foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said, urging Kyiv's backers to do "the opposite". France 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.

events.title: 'What makes China work despite the pain in society?' asks analyst Dan Wang
events.summary: In this edition of Perspective, FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval speaks to Dan Wang, a China expert whose book ‘Breakneck:  China’s Quest to Engineer the Future’ is a New York Times bestseller. It takes a close look at Chinese life and draws from Wang’s own ten years of living there. Wang says the China and the US are some of the most similar people in the world, as they are both hustlers and take shortcuts.

events.title: French 2027 presidential elections: Why Gen Z has mobilised for Mélenchon
events.summary:
🇫🇷 French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc #Mélenchon is both highly controversial and a #GenZ favourite.
 
Mélenchon's young supporters express admiration for his promises to stage a "citizen's revolution",  redistrubute wealth, fight #climatechange and support #Palestine. The candidate's critics have accused him of complancency towards #Russia and antisemitism. 
 
Despite being divisive, recent polls predict that Mélenchon will qualify for the second round of #France's 2027 presidential #election, where he would likely face far-right candidate Marine #LePen.
 
So, why has France's Gen Z mobilised for Mélenchon?
 
🔴 FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler spoke to young voters to find out.

events.title: Should the brakes be put on AI?
events.summary: US President Donald Trump says he is worried about America giving China an edge in the Artificial Intelligence market if too many rules and regulations are put on it. In recent days industry insiders, including top executives at Open AI and Anthropic, have once again sounded the alarm, saying that the way AI is being developed could threaten humanity and calling for more checks to be put in place.

events.title: Trump criticises 'negative forces' seeking to slow AI development
events.summary: US President Donald Trump on Sunday slammed critics of artificial intelligence (AI) who warned firms to slow down development, branding them "negative" forces. The comments came soon after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced his company will not go public this year, citing safety concerns.

events.title: Climate catastrophe leaves Nepal mourning while the search for the missing continues
events.summary: The himalayan flash flood that devastated northern Nepal on August 26 was an unprecedented disaster. The death toll continues to rise, with nearly 1,400 people now confirmed dead and 5,130 still missing, including around 600 foreign nationals from 35 countries.

events.title: Was Russian train strike meant to 'scare' the West?
events.summary: The EU's top diplomat said Monday that Russian strikes which hit a Warsaw-bound train near Ukraine's border with Poland shortly after top Western figures passed through were meant to "scare" off Kyiv's backers. France 24's correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg, has the latest.

events.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with drones as Poland warns of 'escalation'
events.summary: Russia continues its ramped-up air campaign against Ukraine, launching 453 drones in an overnight blitz. One drone struck 800 metres from a border crossing with Poland prompting the polish military to scramble fighter jets and helicopters.

events.title: Thousands rally in support of Brazil's Lula as election campaigning heats up
events.summary: With Brazil set to hold a Presidential election on October 4th, supporters of both incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula Da Silva and his main opponent Flavio Bolsonaro have been taking to the streets. Polls have the candidates, who are on opposite ends of political spectrum, neck and neck.

events.title: Dozens arrested as Turkish police raid LGBTQ bars, activists' homes
events.summary: Turkish police on Sunday made dozens of arrests in a slew of raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists. Authorities said the raids came in the context of the "Decade of the Family" proclaimed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, aimed at "protecting our children, the institution of the family and social order".

events.title: A 'complicated autumn' awaits Sweden after knife-edge vote
events.summary: Sweden's general election remained too close to call early Monday, with nearly 90 percent of votes counted. Four opposition parties led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson held a one-seat parliamentary lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing bloc, which includes the Sweden Democrats, as both leaders said they were ready to govern.

events.title: ‘They drove us from our land’: Thousands displaced by Yemen conflict
events.summary: According to the UN, more than 86,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since July, following fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis rebels and government forces. Many have fled to refugee camps in government-controlled Aden, while others have headed to neighbouring Djibouti.

events.title: Yemen govt forces hit back as conflict with Houthis intensifies
events.summary: The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday, as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighboring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s government. The Yemeni government vowed to send more forces to the Red Sea coast and one official conceded a “painful” defeat last week when Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: 'Palpable tension' as Philippines Muslim region holds first elections
events.summary: A predominantly Muslim region in the southern Philippines held its first parliamentary elections on Monday, seen as a crucial step in the long quest for self-rule after decades of insurgency and violence. Reporting from the region, France 24’s look Jan Camenzind Broomby, takes a look at the vote’s significance, as well as the tensions surrounding election day.

events.title: Retrial over 2018 France terror attack begins
events.summary: The retrial of three defendants linked to a 2018 terror attack in a supermarket in southern France that left four people dead begins in Paris on Monday. The defendants include the former partner of the attacker himself, who was shot dead by the authorities. France 24’s Luke Shrago has more.

events.title: Can Sweden restore welfare system amid increased defense spending?
events.summary: While the results of Sweden's general election remain too close to call, it looks as though the country's center-left opposition may get the chance to form a new government after four years under a right-wing coalition. The runup to the vote was dominated domestic economic issues, including the future of the country's once famously generous welfare state. But Sweden's international financial commitments - notably to increased defense spending following its decision to join NATO amid Russia's war on Ukraine - are likely to limit its options.

events.title: Sweden faces political uncertainty after knife-edge election
events.summary: Sweden was bracing for a protracted struggle to form a government on Monday after election results showed a thin and uncertain lead for the left-wing opposition, while the far-right Sweden Democrats lost ground for the first time since entering parliament 16 years ago.

events.title: Centre-left holds narrow lead in knife-edge Sweden vote
events.summary: Sweden's centre-left opposition on ​Monday looked the most likely to form the next government as preliminary election results showed it holding a narrow three-seat lead over the right-wing ruling parties with most of the votes counted after Sunday's vote. Party leaders, however, have been cautious about claiming victory or accepting defeat with 353 election districts still to be counted ‌and overseas votes not likely to be tallied until Wednesday.

events.title: As Yemen conflict intensifies, Iran the winner?
events.summary: The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday, as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighboring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen’s government. It comes after Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz. The adds pressure on global oil supplies and prices, and that could give Iran leverage in its war with the United States. Andrew Hilliar has more.

events.title: Indonesia: Rescuers resume search for 129 missing after ferry capsized
events.summary: Hundreds of Indonesian rescuers including the coast guard and the navy raced on Monday to board a passenger ship that capsized in the Java Sea over the weekend as they searched for 129 people still missing, officials said, with the confirmed death toll at six.

events.title: 'State-led discrimination': Turkey detains dozens after raids targeting LGBTQ groups
events.summary: Turkish police on Sunday arrested at least 60 people in mass raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ activists, in what authorities said was an operation aimed at boosting traditional family values. The raids sparked condemnation from rights groups and opposition parties, as well as the European Union parliament's rapporteur on Turkey. France 24’s Jasper Mortimer has the latest.

events.title: Who is Iran's 'influential spymaster' Hossein Taeb and does he pull the strings?
events.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, September 14: The New York Times released an exclusive report titled “How Iran’s hard-liners prevailed and sabotaged the US peace deal”. Also: Trump says AI fears are "exaggerated", but reports show a different reality.

events.title: Early results in Swedish election show one-seat advantage for left bloc
events.summary: Preliminary results in Sweden's national election are indicating a narrow one-seat advantage for the left-wing opposition over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing coalition.

events.title: Six dead and search under way for 129 missing from Indonesian passenger ship
events.summary: At least six people have died and 129 people are still missing after a passenger ship in Indonesia carrying more than 240 people lost contact in the Java Sea during bad weather, officials say.

events.title: Drone alert over Lithuania turns out to be flock of birds - as NATO jet scrambled
events.summary: A NATO fighter jet was scrambled after a possible drone sighting in Lithuanian airspace - but it turned out to be a flock of birds.

events.title: Woman, 54, gives birth after using embryo frozen for 22 years
events.summary: A Greek woman has given birth aged 54, beating a government deadline to use one of her embryos, which had been frozen for 22 years.

events.title: Trump calls for Irish reunification - and claims 'it will happen eventually'
events.summary: Donald Trump said he would "love to see" a reunified Ireland, claiming "it's going to happen eventually".

events.title: At least 44 people injured after train derails in northern France
events.summary: A derailed train in northern France left at least 44 people injured, officials said.

events.title: Atlantic Ocean has seen no hurricanes so far this season - this is why
events.summary: Hurricane season has seen an unusually low number of storms forming over the Atlantic - and it's all because of El Nino.

events.title: Five killed and 40 injured in Swiss Alps coach crash
events.summary: Five people have been killed and 40 others injured in a Dutch tour bus crash in eastern Switzerland, police said.

events.title: Deaths in Philippines ferry fire rises to 76
events.summary: A fire that broke out on a passenger ferry in the Philippines has killed at least 76 people, while 13 are still missing.
